title: How a Capacitor Smooths DC Explained Simply | PUC and CBSE
description:
Aarav watches a pump fill the overhead tank in spurts, yet the tap below flows steady. The tank stores water in the spurts and gives it out in the gaps. A rectifier also gives spurts, the humps. Can a capacitor smooth them the same way?

On a live breadboard a capacitor sits across the load of a full-wave rectifier. The oscilloscope shows the input (CH1) and the output (CH2): the diodes charge the capacitor near each peak, switch off, and the capacitor feeds the load in the gap, leaving a small sawtooth ripple. Swap in a bigger capacitor and the ripple shrinks. We derive the ripple voltage V_r = V_m/(2fR_LC) for full-wave and V_m/(fR_LC) for half-wave, then the ideas exams love: R_LC much longer than the gap, full-wave ripple is half, and the ripple factor (1.21 half-wave, 0.48 full-wave, no filter). A worked example, the exam trap (use 2f = 100 Hz for full-wave), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 44 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits (rectifier with capacitor filter).
